描述_ZN: The scroll of "Ink and Vegetable Painting of Xinyi", Ming dynasty, painted by Shen Zhou, paragraph 1, on paper, color on paper, 34.9 cm long, 58.8 cm wide; paragraph 2, on paper, ink and brush, 34.9 cm long, 58.8 cm wide.　　Paragraph 1: This panel is unmarked, with a seal of inscription "Qinan" (in vermilion) at the lower right. There is also a poem inscribed by Wu Kuan: "Half containing a wooden brush, the original name is Xin Yi. A tree under the stone garden increases my thoughts in the old garden." Inscription: "Yanzhou Lai Ji Zi Hou" (in Chinese). Inscription "Xiang Yuanbian Seal" (in vermilion) and other appreciation and collection seals. This painting adopts the boneless method to paint the folding branches of Xin Yi, drawing the flower branches with pale and ancient strokes, painting the petals and leaves with different water colors and inks, with distinct colors and shades and rich layers, and then outlining the leaf tendons with heavy ink and strong and fine strokes. The composition is sparse and dense, and the coloring is clear and elegant, rich in subtlety.　　Paragraph 2: This painting is unmarked, with the seal of "Qinan" in vermilion at the lower right. There is also a poem inscribed by Wu Kuan: "Jade is lush and green at dawn, and the borders are full of spring rain. Bite the roots and do not mangle the leaves, for they can still be cooked in soup." Inscription of "Yuan Bo" in vermilion. It also bears the seal of Xiang Yuanbian, "True Appreciation of Life" in vermilion, and many other marks of appreciation. The painting uses the dry brush with flying white, the rendering of water and ink, and the heavy brush with thick ink to bring an ordinary cabbage to life. The painting highlights the characteristics of calligraphic brushwork, with its roughness and openness, natural twists and turns, and varied use of ink.
